direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale feels like a Mandalorian television special on Disney+ because, while the action sequences are entertaining, the cinematic medium did not provide anything that was different from the show; the direction on a microscale felt pointless and phoned in, especially considering the movie had zero stakes or character development; the storytelling is bad because the whole movie felt like two episodes of the Mandalorian with a Grogu special at the end, where there were no real stakes at all, as it felt like they were just going on missions to check a box; tension is nonexistent considering there are zero stakes in this movie

performance.comments: Basically just plays his stoic character from the show, I would not be surprised if they used a body double for this entire movie and he just recorded his lines at home
He's literally just using his real voice and they distorted it in post
Provides nothing to the movie because it just feels like she's there for her 'Sci-Fi cred', I really hope she got her payday for this role because she was putting. no effort into this role

cast.comments: The cast is filled with a bunch of random characters that really don't add anything to the story; there is really no chemistry in this cast cause it feels like nobody wants to be here

story.comments: The concept genuinely makes me mad because the whole movie is basically two episodes of the Mandalorian with a Grogu special at the end, providing no development for any of the characters in this movie; the plot structure is terrible because the movie is basically just two episodes of the Mandalorian with a Grogu special at the end, making the whole movie feel slow and boring; character writing is bad because there is genuinely no character development for any of these characters, especially for Grogu, because it feels like he is just there for the cute factor and to sell toys

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is bad and phoned in, making it feel like they wrote this script in a week to fulfill their Disney contract; the humor is pretty forced and not really that good; the symbolism is nonexistent considering there are no stakes in this movie; the foreshadowing is bad

score.comments: This is the only genuinely good part of this movie because it really felt innovative and fresh for Star Wars and The Mandalorian, especially with the techno sequences on Shakari; if Ludwig wasted the sauce on this movie and left nothing for The Odyssey, I am going to be LIVID

cinematography.comments: The cinematography honestly felt very dull and uninspired, like every other Disney Star Wars movie; the movie looks and feels like the television show, with the cinematic medium providing nothing new or unique

editing.comments: The movie used many typical Star Wars editing cuts and transitions; the editing felt pretty uninspired as a whole

sound.comments: The sound was pretty standard for a Star Wars movie

visual_effects.comments: The visual effects genuinely felt so dull and bland; the CGI felt very uninspired and boring; this might be the first time I have ever seen bad puppetry because it was so obvious when they were using puppets, especially for Grogu, because it looked so unnatural and clashed with both the real-world actors and the CGI; I would have expected this level of VFX for a Disney+ show but not for a cinematic release, especially considering the $165 million budget

production_design.comments: The production design looked like every other Disney Star Wars property; it looked like an extension of the TV show, and not in a good way, because it does not elevate the source material to the cinematic medium, especially considering the budget

makeup.comments: The makeup felt like an extension of the TV show

costumes.comments: The costumes felt like an extension of the TV show

review.pacing: The pacing is incredibly slow because the movie is basically two episodes of the Mandalorian with a Grogu special at the end, making the whole movie feel like a slog to get through and ultimately boring
review.climax: The climax is your typical action climax, and I was happy because it meant the movie was almost over
review.tone: The tone is that of a very uninspired Star Wars movie
review.overall: Overall, 'The Mandalorian and Grogu' is the most boring Star Wars movie I have ever seen because it is basically just two episodes of the Mandalorian with a Grogu special at the end, not utilizing the cinematic medium and providing zero stakes for these characters; the only redeeming quality of this movie is Ludwig Göransson's score, because it genuinely felt like everyone else involved in this movie was just phoning it in for their Disney paycheck
